# M10-S1: logos next converts a Go module to a loGo/s module with
# byte-span splicing. Plain next prints a unified diff and changes
# nothing; next --fix renames every Go file to .lgo, rewrites err-return
# patterns to ?, Sprintf calls to interpolation, and pure index-range
# append loops to map chains. Complex refactors stay unchanged and land
# in next_tasks.json. Comments and build lines survive byte-identical,
# untouched files survive byte-identical, and the converted module builds
# and tests green under logos, including the local-replace Go import.

env GOPROXY=off
env GOTOOLCHAIN=local

cd m

# The fixture is valid Go before conversion.
logos build ./...
logos test ./...
logos run .
cp stdout $WORK/run-before.txt

# Snapshot every source file; plain next must change nothing.
cp main.go $WORK/main.go.orig
cp convert.go $WORK/convert.go.orig
cp loop.go $WORK/loop.go.orig
cp plain.go $WORK/plain.go.orig
cp gap.go $WORK/gap.go.orig
cp tail.go $WORK/tail.go.orig
cp convert_test.go $WORK/convert_test.go.orig
cp go.mod $WORK/go.mod.orig

# Plain next prints a unified diff and changes nothing (#69, #109).
logos next
stdout '^--- a/convert\.go$'
stdout '^\+\+\+ b/convert\.lgo$'
stdout '^--- a/loop\.go$'
stdout '^\+\+\+ b/loop\.lgo$'
stdout '^--- a/main\.go$'
stdout '^\+\+\+ b/main\.lgo$'
cmp stdout ../want/next.diff
! exists next_tasks.json
! exists main.lgo
cmp main.go $WORK/main.go.orig
cmp convert.go $WORK/convert.go.orig
cmp loop.go $WORK/loop.go.orig
cmp plain.go $WORK/plain.go.orig
cmp gap.go $WORK/gap.go.orig
cmp tail.go $WORK/tail.go.orig
cmp go.mod $WORK/go.mod.orig

# The AI patch plan lists complex refactors without renaming anything.
logos next --ai-patch
exists next_tasks.json
! exists main.lgo
stdout 'ai-patch'
exec rm next_tasks.json

# No logos fmt command exists (#109).
! logos fmt
stderr 'logos fmt: unknown command'

# Fix converts the module.
logos next --fix
stdout 'tasks in next_tasks.json'
exists next_tasks.json
exists main.lgo
exists convert.lgo
exists loop.lgo
exists plain.lgo
exists gap.lgo
exists tail.lgo
exists convert_test.lgo
! exists main.go
! exists convert.go
! exists loop.go
! exists plain.go
! exists gap.go
! exists tail.go
! exists convert_test.go

# Every comment and build line survives byte-identical (#69, #109).
grep '^//go:build linux$' main.lgo
grep 'Command nextdemo exercises logos next migration patterns' main.lgo
grep 'clean input' convert.lgo
grep 'fall back handled below' convert.lgo
grep 'Conversion patterns for index-range append loops' loop.lgo
grep 'Plain helpers stay untouched by conversion' plain.lgo

# Whole-file goldens pin every byte outside the rewrites (#69, #109).
cmp main.lgo ../want/main.lgo
cmp convert.lgo ../want/convert.lgo
cmp gap.lgo $WORK/gap.go.orig
cmp loop.lgo ../want/loop.lgo
cmp tail.lgo ../want/tail.lgo

# The task plan matches the schema, spans, and rules exactly.
cmp next_tasks.json ../want/next_tasks.json

# Error patterns became ?.
grep 'v := clean\(s\)\? // clean input' convert.lgo
grep 'v = clean\(s\)\?' convert.lgo
grep 'check\(n\)\?' main.lgo
# main returns no error, so its own check stays as written.
grep 'if err != nil' main.lgo

# Sprintf with only s d v operands became interpolation.
grep '\$"hello \{msg\} \{n\} \{true\}"' main.lgo
! grep 'Sprintf' main.lgo

# The pure index-range append loop became a map chain.
grep 'ys := xs\.map\(x => double\(x\)\)' loop.lgo

# A pure loop whose declaration is not adjacent stays byte-identical: the
# statement between them survives (gap.lgo is byte-identical, checked with
# the goldens above) and nothing is rewritten or listed.
! grep 'spaced' next_tasks.json
# A target accumulated before the loop is listed, not rewritten.
grep -count=1 '^\tys := \[\]int\{\}$' loop.lgo
grep -count=1 '^\t\tys = append\(ys, double\(xs\[i\]\)\)$' loop.lgo

# Complex refactors stayed unchanged and are listed for AI patching.
grep 'fetch fallback for' convert.lgo
grep 'return v, err' convert.lgo
grep 'hex %x' convert.lgo
grep 'break' loop.lgo
grep 'n\+\+' loop.lgo
grep '"version": "logos-next-1"' next_tasks.json
grep -count=5 '"category": "ai-patch"' next_tasks.json
grep 'func fetch\(s string\) \(string, error\)' next_tasks.json
grep 'func probe\(s string\) \(string, error\)' next_tasks.json
grep 'func firstBig\(xs \[\]int, limit int\) \[\]int' next_tasks.json
grep 'func countNeg\(xs \[\]int\) \(int, \[\]int\)' next_tasks.json
grep 'func seeded\(xs \[\]int\) \[\]int' next_tasks.json
grep '"rule": "err-return"' next_tasks.json
grep '"rule": "loop-chain"' next_tasks.json
grep '"file": "convert.lgo"' next_tasks.json
grep '"file": "loop.lgo"' next_tasks.json
grep '"verification_cmd": "logos build \./\.\.\."' next_tasks.json

# The local-replace Go import stays as written (R-U2).
grep 'example\.com/dep/greet' main.lgo

# Untouched code is byte-identical apart from the rename.
cmp plain.lgo $WORK/plain.go.orig
cmp convert_test.lgo $WORK/convert_test.go.orig

# The converted module builds, tests, and runs identically under logos.
# loop.lgo sorts after the synthetic logos-chain base file, so this build
# covers the chain lowering positions under DWARF scope checks.
logos build ./...
logos test ./...
logos run .
cmp stdout $WORK/run-before.txt
stdout '^hello \[logos\] 3 true$'
stdout '^hex ff$'
stdout '^\[2 4 6\]$'
stdout '^\[1\]$'
stdout '^2 \[-1 2\]$'
stdout '^\[2 4\] 2$'
stdout '^\[0 6\]$'

-- m/go.mod --
module example.com/next

go 1.27

require example.com/dep v0.0.0

replace example.com/dep v0.0.0 => ../dep

-- m/main.go --
//go:build linux

// Command nextdemo exercises logos next migration patterns.
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"example.com/dep/greet"
)

// check validates the limit.
func check(n int) error {
	if n < 0 {
		return fmt.Errorf("negative limit %d", n)
	}
	return nil
}

// apply checks the limit and greets.
func apply(name string, n int) (string, error) {
	if err := check(n); err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	msg := greet.Tag(name)
	return fmt.Sprintf("hello %s %d %v", msg, n, true), nil
}

func main() {
	msg, err := apply("logos", 3)
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Println("error:", err)
		return
	}
	fmt.Println(msg)
	fmt.Println(hex(255))
	fmt.Println(doubleAll([]int{1, 2, 3}))
	fmt.Println(firstBig([]int{1, 5, 2}, 3))
	n, out := countNeg([]int{-1, 2})
	fmt.Println(n, out)
	fmt.Println(spaced([]int{1, 2}))
	fmt.Println(seeded([]int{3}))
}

-- m/convert.go --
// Conversion patterns for error returns and formatting.
package main

import "fmt"

// clean rejects empty input.
func clean(s string) (string, error) {
	if s == "" {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("empty input")
	}
	return s, nil
}

// load cleans the raw input before use.
func load(s string) (string, error) {
	v, err := clean(s) // clean input
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	return v, nil
}

// reuse assigns into existing variables.
func reuse(s string) (string, error) {
	v := ""
	v, err := clean(s)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	return v, nil
}

// fetch loads with a fallback note on failure.
func fetch(s string) (string, error) {
	w, err := clean(s)
	// fall back handled below
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Println("fetch fallback for", s)
		return "", err
	}
	return w, nil
}

// probe keeps the error for reporting.
func probe(s string) (string, error) {
	v, err := clean(s)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	return v, err
}

// hex formats n as hexadecimal for logs.
func hex(n int) string {
	return fmt.Sprintf("hex %x", n)
}

-- m/loop.go --
// Conversion patterns for index-range append loops.
package main

// double doubles n.
func double(n int) int {
	return n * 2
}

// doubleAll doubles every element.
func doubleAll(xs []int) []int {
	var ys []int
	for i := 0; i < len(xs); i++ {
		ys = append(ys, double(xs[i]))
	}
	return ys
}

// firstBig collects elements up to the limit.
func firstBig(xs []int, limit int) []int {
	var out []int
	for i := 0; i < len(xs); i++ {
		if xs[i] > limit {
			break
		}
		out = append(out, xs[i])
	}
	return out
}

// countNeg counts and collects negative elements.
func countNeg(xs []int) (int, []int) {
	var out []int
	n := 0
	for i := 0; i < len(xs); i++ {
		n++
		out = append(out, xs[i])
	}
	return n, out
}

// seeded accumulates into the target before the loop.
func seeded(xs []int) []int {
	ys := []int{}
	ys = append(ys, 0)
	for i := 0; i < len(xs); i++ {
		ys = append(ys, double(xs[i]))
	}
	return ys
}

-- m/gap.go --
// Gap keeps an unrelated statement between a declaration and its loop.
package main

// spaced keeps an unrelated statement between the declaration and the loop.
func spaced(xs []int) ([]int, int) {
	var ys []int
	size := len(xs)
	for i := 0; i < len(xs); i++ {
		ys = append(ys, double(xs[i]))
	}
	return ys, size
}

-- m/tail.go --
// Tail ends its file with a rewrite so the diff context stops at the last line.
package main

import "strconv"

// parse converts text to a number.
func parse(s string) (int, error) {
	n, err := strconv.Atoi(s)
	if err != nil {
		return 0, err
	}
	return n, nil
}
-- m/plain.go --
// Plain helpers stay untouched by conversion.
package main

// identity returns n unchanged.
func identity(n int) int {
	return n
}

-- m/convert_test.go --
package main

import "testing"

// TestDoubleAll pins the converted map chain behavior.
func TestDoubleAll(t *testing.T) {
	got := doubleAll([]int{1, 2, 3})
	want := []int{2, 4, 6}
	if len(got) != len(want) {
		t.Fatalf("len = %d, want %d", len(got), len(want))
	}
	for i := range want {
		if got[i] != want[i] {
			t.Fatalf("got[%d] = %d, want %d", i, got[i], want[i])
		}
	}
}

// TestFirstBig pins the loop left for AI patching.
func TestFirstBig(t *testing.T) {
	got := firstBig([]int{1, 5, 2}, 3)
	if len(got) != 1 || got[0] != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("got %v, want [1]", got)
	}
}

// TestCountNeg pins the loop left for AI patching.
func TestCountNeg(t *testing.T) {
	n, out := countNeg([]int{-1, 2})
	if n != 2 || len(out) != 2 || out[0] != -1 || out[1] != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("got %d %v, want 2 [-1 2]", n, out)
	}
}

-- want/main.lgo --
//go:build linux

// Command nextdemo exercises logos next migration patterns.
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"example.com/dep/greet"
)

// check validates the limit.
func check(n int) error {
	if n < 0 {
		return fmt.Errorf("negative limit %d", n)
	}
	return nil
}

// apply checks the limit and greets.
func apply(name string, n int) (string, error) {
	check(n)?
	msg := greet.Tag(name)
	return $"hello {msg} {n} {true}", nil
}

func main() {
	msg, err := apply("logos", 3)
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Println("error:", err)
		return
	}
	fmt.Println(msg)
	fmt.Println(hex(255))
	fmt.Println(doubleAll([]int{1, 2, 3}))
	fmt.Println(firstBig([]int{1, 5, 2}, 3))
	n, out := countNeg([]int{-1, 2})
	fmt.Println(n, out)
	fmt.Println(spaced([]int{1, 2}))
	fmt.Println(seeded([]int{3}))
}

-- want/convert.lgo --
// Conversion patterns for error returns and formatting.
package main

import "fmt"

// clean rejects empty input.
func clean(s string) (string, error) {
	if s == "" {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("empty input")
	}
	return s, nil
}

// load cleans the raw input before use.
func load(s string) (string, error) {
	v := clean(s)? // clean input
	return v, nil
}

// reuse assigns into existing variables.
func reuse(s string) (string, error) {
	v := ""
	v = clean(s)?
	return v, nil
}

// fetch loads with a fallback note on failure.
func fetch(s string) (string, error) {
	w, err := clean(s)
	// fall back handled below
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Println("fetch fallback for", s)
		return "", err
	}
	return w, nil
}

// probe keeps the error for reporting.
func probe(s string) (string, error) {
	v, err := clean(s)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	return v, err
}

// hex formats n as hexadecimal for logs.
func hex(n int) string {
	return fmt.Sprintf("hex %x", n)
}

-- want/loop.lgo --
// Conversion patterns for index-range append loops.
package main

// double doubles n.
func double(n int) int {
	return n * 2
}

// doubleAll doubles every element.
func doubleAll(xs []int) []int {
	ys := xs.map(x => double(x))
	return ys
}

// firstBig collects elements up to the limit.
func firstBig(xs []int, limit int) []int {
	var out []int
	for i := 0; i < len(xs); i++ {
		if xs[i] > limit {
			break
		}
		out = append(out, xs[i])
	}
	return out
}

// countNeg counts and collects negative elements.
func countNeg(xs []int) (int, []int) {
	var out []int
	n := 0
	for i := 0; i < len(xs); i++ {
		n++
		out = append(out, xs[i])
	}
	return n, out
}

// seeded accumulates into the target before the loop.
func seeded(xs []int) []int {
	ys := []int{}
	ys = append(ys, 0)
	for i := 0; i < len(xs); i++ {
		ys = append(ys, double(xs[i]))
	}
	return ys
}

// Package greet helps the next test with a local Go dependency.
package greet

// Tag wraps s in brackets.
func Tag(s string) string {
	return "[" + s + "]"
}
